sections.heading: Saying your name
sections.body:
The most common way to give your name is *Me llamo…* (literally "I call myself…"): *Me llamo Ana.* You can also say *Soy Ana* (I'm Ana) or, a bit more formally, *Mi nombre es Ana* (My name is Ana).

To ask someone's name:

- *¿Cómo te llamas?* — What's your name? (informal, to a friend, a child, someone your age)
- *¿Cómo se llama usted?* — What's your name? (formal)
- *¿Cómo se llama?* — What's his/her name? (about someone else)

sections.heading: Nice to meet you
sections.body:
When you meet someone, say *Mucho gusto* (Nice to meet you) or *Encantado* (if you're a man) / *Encantada* (if you're a woman). The other person usually answers *Igualmente* (Likewise) or *El gusto es mío* (The pleasure is mine).

To introduce someone else, say *Te presento a…* (informal) or *Le presento a…* (formal): *Te presento a Carlos.* (This is Carlos. / Let me introduce Carlos.) You can also simply say *Este es Carlos* (for a man) or *Esta es Ana* (for a woman).

sections.heading: Tú or usted?
sections.body:
Spanish has two words for "you" when talking to one person:

- *tú* — informal: friends, family, children, people your age in casual settings.
- *usted* — formal and respectful: older people, strangers, customers, officials, your boss.

In Latin America, *usted* is used more than in Spain; when in doubt with an adult you don't know, start with *usted*. If they say *Puedes tutearme* (you can use *tú* with me), switch to *tú*. In some countries, such as Colombia and Costa Rica, *usted* is used even among friends and family.

The verb changes with the pronoun: *¿Cómo te llamas?* goes with *tú*; *¿Cómo se llama usted?* goes with *usted*.

sections.heading: Where are you from?
sections.body:
Two quick questions you will hear right after names:

- *¿De dónde eres?* — Where are you from? (informal)
- *¿De dónde es usted?* — Where are you from? (formal)

Answer with *Soy de* + place: *Soy de Chicago.* *Soy de México.* You'll learn much more about this in the next lesson.

examples: Hola, me llamo Ana. ¿Cómo te llamas?
Hi, my name is Ana. What's your name?
My name is Carlos. Nice to meet you.
Pleased to meet you. (said by a woman)
Pleased to meet you. (said by a man)
Le presento a la señora Díaz.
Este es Carlos y esta es Ana.
This is Carlos and this is Ana.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask a new classmate their name?
How do you politely ask an older stranger their name?
Ana (a woman) is introduced to someone. What does she say?
Someone says *Mucho gusto.* A natural reply is…
Which "you" do you use with your new boss?
Which "you" do you use with a five-year-old child?
What does *Me llamo Pedro* literally mean?
How do you introduce your friend Luis to your friend Sara?
exercises.explain: Sara is a friend, so use the informal *te*.

exercises.prompt: In Latin America, when you meet an adult stranger, the safe choice is…
Put the words in order: "Hi, my name is Ana. What's your name?"
exercises.answer: Hola, me llamo Ana. ¿Cómo te llamas?

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Good morning, what's your name?" (formal)
